meta.name: Spring Documentation RAG Evaluation Set · HARD
meta.relation_to_easy_set: h01-h15 correspond one-to-one with f01/f02/f05/f06/f08/f10/f12/f13/f14/f15/f17/m02/m10/m13/m15 in questions.json; the score difference between the two sets is the inflation caused by question leakage.
how_to_judge: Always report Recall@1 (Recall@3 saturates on the easy set; only Recall@1 is discriminative).
For multi-hop questions, report both hit-any and hit-all (questions like h17 require both sources to be hit to count as complete).
Add a score column in the CSV (used for setting the refusal threshold).
Hit criterion: sourcePath matches file AND gold section is a prefix/contained in the chunk heading_path.
This set does not include refuse questions; refusal capability is still judged using the 17 refuse questions in questions.json.

judge_rules.h16: Precise-location question: the terms Prototype/Lookup are intentionally omitted from the question; retrieve by semantics.
judge_rules.h17: Same-title section distractor: both files contain a section with the same title; requires exact file+section match (recommended to judge by hit-all).
judge_rules.h21: Precise-location question: the annotation name is intentionally omitted from the question; retrieve by semantics.
judge_rules.h23: Colloquial phrasing question: the term UriComponents does not appear in the question (it appears only in the answer).
judge_rules.h24: Colloquial phrasing question: title words such as Testing / Running Server must not appear in the question.
judge_rules.h25: Corpus-boundary question: only implementations listed in this section count; listing vector stores outside the corpus counts as wrong.

meta.expectation: Hard set scores should be clearly lower than the easy set (otherwise the questions are still too shallow).

questions.question: I want to initiate a model chat call in my project. How do I typically obtain the entry-point object, and what are the ways to create it?
key_points: Customize an injected ChatClient.Builder and call build().
Alternatively, create it directly via static methods such as ChatClient.create(chatModel).

gold_source.section: Chat Client API > Creating a ChatClient

questions.question: I want to insert several pieces of processing logic before and after a model request. What determines the order in which these logics run, and what are the key classes that make up this mechanism?
key_points: Non-streaming: CallAdvisor / CallAdvisorChain; streaming: StreamAdvisor / StreamAdvisorChain.
Request and response objects: ChatClientRequest / ChatClientResponse, which can share an advisor context.
getOrder() determines the execution order in the chain; smaller values run first.

questions.question: I only want to retrieve within documents from one specific source. How do I restrict the search scope?
key_points: Pass a filter expression (e.g. module == 'x') together with the similarity search request to the VectorStore.
Metadata is written on the Document, and is matched by the expression at retrieval time.

questions.question: I want to load a batch of documents into a vector store for question answering. Where should the out-of-the-box dependencies, connection, and dimension configuration go, and what are they?
key_points: Add the pgvector vector store starter dependency.
Configuration items live under spring.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.* (e.g. schema initialization, dimensions, index type, etc.).

questions.question: There is a group of my own configuration items in the configuration file. How do I bind them in code using a Java class and also perform validation along the way?
key_points: Annotate the class with @ConfigurationProperties, together with @EnableConfigurationProperties / @ConfigurationPropertiesScan or registering it as a bean.
Relaxed binding is supported (kebab-case in the configuration file can bind to camelCase fields).

questions.question: Logs from many third-party components are too noisy. I don't want to write one logger per package. Can I adjust their levels in groups all at once?
key_points: Define log groups with logging.group.<name>.
Then set the level for the whole group with logging.level.<group-name>.

questions.question: I want to initialize a connection pool when an object is created and release resources when it is destroyed. What are the ways to write this?
key_points: Annotation approach: @PostConstruct / @PreDestroy.
Interface approach: InitializingBean / DisposableBean.
Declarative approach: @Bean(initMethod=..., destroyMethod=...).

gold_source.section: Customizing the Nature of a Bean > Lifecycle Callbacks

questions.question: The framework provides extension points after an object is instantiated and before/after initialization. I want to wrap the object there (e.g. with a proxy). Which interface should I implement, and which of the two callbacks runs first?
key_points: Insert custom logic after bean instantiation and before/after initialization (two callbacks: before/after initialization).
A typical use is wrapping or proxying beans (for example, AOP proxies are produced at this layer).

gold_source.section: Container Extension Points > Customizing Beans by Using a `BeanPostProcessor`

questions.question: There is a scope where every retrieval creates a new instance. Who is responsible for recycling and cleaning up these instances?
key_points: Every request for that bean creates a new instance (both injection and getBean create a new one).
Spring does not manage the full lifecycle of prototype beans: configured destruction callbacks are not called, and the caller must clean up itself.

questions.question: When an inner method fails and rolls back, I don't want it to affect the outer result that has already been committed. How should the annotation be set? Will the inner and outer transactions affect each other?
key_points: Use an independent physical transaction for each transaction scope, never participating in an existing outer transaction.
The inner and outer transactions can commit or roll back independently; the outer is not affected by an inner rollback, and inner locks are released immediately after completion.
The inner transaction can declare its own isolation level/timeout/read-only and does not inherit from the outer.
The documentation warns: the inner transaction occupies an extra connection, and abuse may exhaust the connection pool or even cause deadlocks.

questions.question: An endpoint needs to wait for an asynchronous result before returning. How do I release the request-handling thread first and respond only when the result arrives?
key_points: Take request handling off the Servlet container thread to avoid occupying the thread for a long time.
The controller returns a DeferredResult; after the backend thread completes its sequence, setResult triggers the response.

questions.question: I want to load documents into a vector store. How do I handle table creation and vector length (dimensions) so that I don't have to create them manually?
key_points: In the pgvector auto-configuration, schema initialization can be enabled.
The dimensions must match the output dimensions of the embedding model being used.
This configuration item affects both table creation and subsequent inserts/retrieval.

questions.question: I want to insert my own logic into the model call chain (logging elapsed time or rewriting the request both work). What methods do I need to implement, and how do I call the next node in the chain?
key_points: Implement the CallAdvisor / StreamAdvisor interface and provide getName() and getOrder().
In adviseCall/adviseStream, process the request, call the next entity in the chain as needed, and finally process the response.
The request/response objects carry a shareable context.

questions.question: The framework provides two extension points at different stages: one can modify configuration metadata before an object is created, and the other can wrap an object after it is instantiated. When does each of them take effect?
key_points: BeanFactoryPostProcessor works at the bean-definition stage: it can read and modify configuration metadata (bean definitions).
BeanPostProcessor works after instantiation: it can wrap/proxy instances and affect behavior before and after initialization.
Typical uses: AOP proxies, annotation processing, property-injection enhancement.

gold_source.section: Container Extension Points > Customizing Beans by Using a `BeanPostProcessor`
Container Extension Points > Customizing Configuration Metadata with a `BeanFactoryPostProcessor`

questions.question: Browser cross-origin requests are blocked, and after a reverse proxy the protocol and domain received are incorrect. Which two built-in framework components handle these two things respectively?
key_points: CORS: preflight and response-header handling for cross-origin requests.
Forwarded Headers: correctly restore the original request's host/protocol/port behind a reverse proxy.

questions.question: An object that should be newly created every time is injected into a long-lived object, but I find I always get the same old instance. How can I make it be recreated on every call?
key_points: The container can override a method on a container-managed bean so that it returns a lookup result for another bean (Lookup Method Injection).
Under the hood it uses CGLIB to dynamically generate a subclass that overrides the method.
Limitation: neither the overridden class nor the method may be final.

questions.question: Both filter retrieval results by field. How should the Qdrant and PGVector stores each do this?
key_points: Both use the same generic metadata filter expression (filterExpression).
The syntax is the same, but they belong to the respective sections of the two stores.

questions.question: I want to run an open-source model locally. What are the prerequisites, and in which class are the tunable runtime options located?
key_points: Prerequisites: install Ollama locally, or run it via Testcontainers; and pull the model you want to use.
Runtime options are provided by OllamaChatOptions (model, temperature, thinking mode, etc.); the older OllamaOptions is deprecated.

questions.question: How do I enable auto-configuration for storing vectors in Redis? And which section covers table creation and initialization?
key_points: The Redis vector store provides Spring Boot auto-configuration; just add the corresponding starter.
Schema initialization is a general vector-store topic, controlled by a configuration item that decides whether tables/indexes are created automatically.

questions.question: Which starter should be added for the MCP client and which for the MCP server respectively? How is the server protocol specified?
key_points: Client: spring-ai-starter-mcp-client (supports STDIO / SSE / Streamable-HTTP and other transports).
Server: spring-ai-starter-mcp-server, with spring.ai.mcp.server.protocol specifying the protocol/transport.

gold_source.section: MCP Server Boot Starter > MCP Server Boot Starters

questions.question: An application has two data sources and two transaction managers. How do I indicate on a method which one to use?
key_points: The annotation's value / transactionManager attribute can specify which transaction manager to use.
The value can be the bean name of the transaction manager, or a @Qualifier value.

questions.question: After a method returns normally, and when it throws an exception, I want to execute different processing logic respectively. Which advice types in an aspect correspond to these, and which annotations are used for each?
key_points: Executed on normal return: @AfterReturning.
Executed on exit by exception: @AfterThrowing.

questions.question: I need to build a link that contains path variables and may also contain Chinese characters and spaces, and return it to the frontend. How do I encode it so it does not break or get truncated?
key_points: UriComponentsBuilder has two levels of encoding: encode() first encodes the template, then strictly encodes variables when they are expanded.
UriComponents.encode() encodes after variable expansion; both convert non-ASCII and illegal characters into escaped bytes.
The choice depends on whether characters with reserved meaning in the path (e.g. ;) need to be preserved.

questions.question: In a concurrent scenario, I want the application to actually listen on a port and then send HTTP requests to verify it. What is the officially recommended way to write this?
key_points: Use @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT) to start a real server on a random port.
Inject the actual port with @LocalServerPort; to send requests, autowire RestTestClient (together with @AutoConfigureRestTestClient).

gold_source.section: Testing Spring Boot Applications > Testing With a Running Server

questions.question: Which vector databases does Spring AI support? (List only those actually covered in the documentation.)
key_points: Only list the implementations covered in this section (Azure, Apache Cassandra, Chroma, Elasticsearch, GemFire, etc.).
Do not list other vector stores from training knowledge as if they were in the documentation — this is a corpus-boundary question.
